context: These studies examine social-emotional learning, self-regulation and tutoring in other programs and settings. They support the components we draw on; they did not evaluate NLU’s Therapy + Tutoring program. Individual results vary.

studies.heading: Learning includes emotional skills
studies.title: The Impact of Enhancing Students’ Social and Emotional Learning: A Meta-Analysis of School-Based Universal Interventions
studies.finding: Across 213 school-based studies involving 270,034 students, social-emotional learning programs improved social-emotional skills, behavior and academic performance compared with controls.
studies.limit: These were universal school programs, not a trial of outpatient counseling combined with tutoring. Implementation and program design matter.

studies.heading: Regulation skills can develop
studies.title: Effectiveness of Universal Self-regulation–Based Interventions in Children and Adolescents: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
studies.finding: A review of 49 randomized trials found that a range of interventions improved self-regulation. Of 13 studies reporting academic achievement, 11 reported positive results and two found no effect.
studies.limit: Participants were ages 2–17, mostly younger children. Programs varied, and only a subset measured academic outcomes; improvement is not assured for every child.

studies.heading: Academic instruction still matters
studies.citation: Nickow, Oreopoulos and Quan · American Educational Research Journal · 2024
studies.title: The Promise of Tutoring for PreK–12 Learning: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of the Experimental Evidence
studies.finding: A meta-analysis of randomized tutoring experiments found positive learning effects overall. Effects tended to be larger with teachers or paraprofessionals, earlier grades, and tutoring at least three days a week during school.
studies.limit: This research evaluated tutoring, not NLU’s combined model. Results from frequent school-day tutoring cannot be promised for a weekly or shorter session.
